Requirements/Graph visualization in a React application

Requirement · high criticality

Graph visualization in a React application

Render and interact with graph data in a React application. The NVL suite was the initial candidate; after it failed the licence constraint, open-source alternatives were reviewed. Choose a renderer with layouts, interaction handling and React integration.

Owner: dbs-amoswongCadence: 90 daysCreated 28 Oct 20269 candidates
Decision ApprovedActive

Adopt cytoscape

Best fit for Neo4j-style graph exploration: MIT, zero dependencies, SLSA provenance, active, 15.8M weekly downloads, 138 KB gzip. Layouts come via extensions; the React wrapper is stale, so use the core API with a ref or a thin internal wrapper.

Build vs buy scores the capability, not this package. A rejected package can still be a capability worth buying from a maintained alternative.

Constraints

  • Permissive license across the full dependency tree
  • React 18 and 19 supported
  • No install scripts in the dependency tree
  • No unfixed high or critical advisories
  • Actively maintained (release within 12 months)
  • Compatible versions across the chosen graph stack
  • If npm provenance is unavailable, pin exact versions and record the gap

Out of scope

  • Backend graph database and query language
  • Visual design and theming
  • Detailed benchmark against every non-NVL graph library

Decision rationale

The NVL suite is denied: its LICENSE.txt limits use to Neo4j Aura or commercial Neo4j, it publishes no repository, carries no provenance and cannot be loaded by Node in either module system. 1.2.2 was checked separately: same licence and packaging, different layout stack, so the denial applies to both. Adopt Cytoscape.js as the primary renderer: MIT, zero dependencies, SLSA provenance, active, 138 KB gzip, and layouts via extensions. Use the core API with a ref or a thin internal wrapper because react-cytoscapejs is stale. Adopt Sigma.js as the fallback for large graphs: MIT, WebGL, 110 KB gzip and active, but client-only (WebGL2) and without provenance; pair it with graphology and @react-sigma/core. Hold @antv/g6 (88 MB, 104 packages, 413 KB gzip, 333 open issues, no release in 90 days) and @xyflow/react (excellent node editor, but not an exploration or layout engine).

Review timeline

  1. 28 Oct 2026 @neo4j-nvl/base Avoid Avoid. The renderer behind the suite: proprietary licence, no source, no provenance, 13 pinned dependencies including a Segment analytics SDK, and it touches document at import time.
  2. 28 Oct 2026 @neo4j-nvl/react Avoid Avoid. Proprietary licence, no published repository, no provenance, and a package that Node cannot load in either module system. The React binding is small; the cost is a 53 MB tree and a legal constraint.
  3. 28 Oct 2026 @neo4j-nvl/interaction-handlers Avoid Avoid. A 222 KB interaction layer over the proprietary renderer, with the same licence, source and provenance gaps and the same bundler-only packaging.
  4. 28 Oct 2026 @neo4j-nvl/layout-workers Avoid Avoid as part of the suite. Small and technically the cleanest package, but it carries the same proprietary licence, no source and no provenance. It depends on upstream @dagrejs/dagre, not the Neo4j fork.
  5. 28 Oct 2026 @neo4j-bloom/dagre Avoid Not needed. MIT and public, but a 1-star fork of dagrejs/dagre pinned at 3.1.1 while upstream is 3.1.3, and it is not used by the NVL layout-workers package. Use @dagrejs/dagre directly.
  6. 28 Oct 2026 @antv/g6 Hold Feature-rich AntV graph engine, MIT and capable, but 88 MB and 104 packages installed, 413 KB gzip, 333 open issues and no release in 90 days. Hold unless you specifically need its layout or analysis features.
  7. 28 Oct 2026 @xyflow/react Hold Excellent node/edge editor with first-class React and provenance, but it is not a graph exploration engine: no built-in force or dagre layout, and you would add those yourself. Hold for this requirement; adopt it for workflow or editor UIs.
  8. 28 Oct 2026 sigma Adopt WebGL renderer for large graphs, with the graphology ecosystem. MIT, active, 110 KB gzip, 6.9 MB and 10 packages. No provenance, and it needs WebGL2 and browser globals at import, so use it only in client components.
  9. 28 Oct 2026 cytoscape Adopt Best fit for Neo4j-style graph exploration: MIT, zero dependencies, SLSA provenance, active, 15.8M weekly downloads, 138 KB gzip. Layouts come via extensions; the React wrapper is stale, so use the core API with a ref or a thin internal wrapper.
